correctness.rationale: For a nondegenerate monotone log-concave law with contiguous positive support of exactly N=2,3,4,5 integer atoms, reflection and translation allow positive decreasing masses. The paired monotonicity inequality gives mean μ≤(N−1)/2. N=2 and N=3 therefore always include the mode among the mean-adjacent masses (uniform N=3 included). For N=4 the nontrivial μ≥1 condition for successive ratios 1≥a≥b≥c>0 is ab(1+2c)≥1; hence a²(1+2a)≥1 and R=a≥r4. For N=5 it is ab(1+2c+3cd)≥1, giving a²(1+2a+3a²)≥1 and R=a≥r5. The defining polynomials have unique positive roots in (0,1), with equality forcing all successive ratios equal: the normalized truncated geometric sequence, up to translation/reflection. At μ=1 the mean-adjacent ratio is exactly the claimed a, so boundaries and attainment are correct. Independent new finite rational-ratio grid and high-precision root/equality-mean tests corroborate but do not prove the all-law bounds.

originality.rationale: The precise new facts are r4≈0.6572981061 and r5≈0.5677373609, the sharp finite-support mean-neighbor/mode ratios, and their rigid geometric equality cases. Melbourne–Palafox-Castillo Corollary 2.8 proves only the weaker universal e^(−1) bound for unbounded-support discrete log-concave laws. value.rationale: Mean mass versus modal mass is a natural operational concentration measure. Four atoms is the first support length where the mode can be excluded from the two mean-adjacent masses; five is the last length before the second interior mean cell can activate. The exact algebraic sharp thresholds and rigid equality profiles classify this motivated finite regime; this is more than generic log-affine renaming.

limitations: Only monotone (not all) log-concave integer laws with contiguous support sizes 2–5 are claimed.
